newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude down, Minas and Duri trade at -15 cts.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude down, Minas and Duri trade at -15 cts.

text.p: Asian crude prices were slightly lower on Thursday as physical trade ticked over quietly in the absence of Japanese players.

Traders said Minas and Duri have traded at 15 cents below the ICP this week, reflecting the lack of demand for the crudes. Minas changed hands between majors, while an affiliate sold the Duri to a blender, the traders said.
Traders said most interest for heavier sweet grades was in the second half of April and not for early dates, reflecting the lack of bids in the market.
Producers were offering Minas at flat.
Traders said China and Japan were relaxed in their buying needs and were not expected to be major buyers until the second half of the trading month.
But the return of the 125,000-bpd Balongan refinery last week and the expected restart of the 120,000 bpd Dumai refinery on Friday should offer Minas and Duri some support.

Dubai and Brent paper levels in Asia were mostly steady with May Brent/Dubai indicated at $1.53/$1.60 per barrel, while May/June Dubai spreads were indicated at 15/22 cents, both spreads little changed on a day earlier.
